# test_deduplicate_sorted.py
import pytest

from your_module import deduplicate_sorted  # Replace with the actual module name


# Happy paths
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("lst", "expected"),
    [
        ([1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3]),
        ([-2, -2, -1, 0, 0, 5, 5], [-2, -1, 0, 5]),
        (["a", "a", "b", "b", "c"], ["a", "b", "c"]),
        ([0, 0, 1, 1], [0, 1]),
        ([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3]),
    ],
)
def test_deduplicate_sorted_happy_paths(lst, expected):
    assert deduplicate_sorted(lst) == expected


# Edge cases
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("lst", "expected"),
    [
        ([], []),
        ([42], [42]),
        ([7, 7, 7], [7]),
        ([[1], [1], [2], [2]], [[1], [2]]),  # unhashable but comparable items
    ],
)
def test_deduplicate_sorted_edge_cases(lst, expected):
    assert deduplicate_sorted(lst) == expected


def test_deduplicate_sorted_does_not_mutate_input():
    lst = [1, 1, 2, 2, 3]
    original = lst.copy()

    result = deduplicate_sorted(lst)

    assert result == [1, 2, 3]
    assert lst == original


def test_only_removes_adjacent_duplicates_when_input_is_not_sorted():
    # The function assumes sorted input and only removes consecutive duplicates.
    assert deduplicate_sorted([1, 2, 1, 1, 3, 2]) == [1, 2, 1, 3, 2]


# Error cases
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "bad_input",
    [
        pytest.param(1, id="int"),
        pytest.param(object(), id="plain-object"),
        pytest.param(iter([1, 1]), id="iterator"),
    ],
)
def test_truthy_non_indexable_input_raises_type_error(bad_input):
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        deduplicate_sorted(bad_input)


def test_comparison_errors_are_propagated():
    class ExplodingComparison:
        def __ne__(self, other):
            raise ValueError("comparison failed")

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="comparison failed"):
        deduplicate_sorted([ExplodingComparison(), ExplodingComparison()])
